decisions.reason: The downward pour direction does not change the platform height, footprint, supported cup size, or its purpose of providing clearance beneath the spouts.
Spout pour direction does not alter the requirement that the dispensing path be removable or easy to clean.
The source changes spout orientation but does not change the required leak-free seals or plumbing behavior.

The controlled-dispensing requirement remains valid unchanged; downward orientation is an independently represented spout-geometry constraint rather than a change to its valve, sequence, flow-control, or operator-control attributes.
Changing the pour direction does not modify the requirement to prevent liquid from entering the base or electrical components.
The client does not request a different dispensing component or a BOM revision; the existing solenoid-valve selection remains unchanged.
The consistency statement explains the downward spout orientation but does not change the mixing or frothing acceptance criteria, whisk selection, or whisk positioning.
Spout orientation has no stated effect on electrical loads, power-supply capacity, motor controllers, or overload margin.
The source changes spout pour direction and does not alter bowl capacity, depth, enclosure-size constraints, or bowl geometry.
The downward spout direction does not change the placement of speed controls, dispense buttons, or the master power control.
The source does not change placard wording, position, duplication, or viewing orientation.
The source attributes downward pouring to drink consistency and does not establish a new splash-control target or mitigation method.
